Anya (PM): quick sync — we need final acceptance criteria for SLOs/error budgets and canary/fallback policy for the v0.9 rollout. customer asks (enterprise) require predictable tail latency. proposing defaults below, open to pushback

Anya (PM): proposed SLOs:
```
P50 <= 40ms
P95 <= 200ms
P99 <= 800ms
Availability >= 99.9% (monthly)
Error budget: 0.1% requests/day (soft), 0.5% requests/week (hard)
```

Jordan (Product): looks reasonable as a starting point. need to call out acceptable graceful-degrade behaviors in PRD — e.g., fallback to cached responses, model-variant routing, or partial output with explanation. customers expect clear semantics.

Sam (SRE): two immediate asks: 1) P99=800ms might be tight for long-context in some regions; suggest we make P99 per-route and per-sequence-length. 2) define error budget burn policies + automated rollback thresholds. e.g., if burn rate > 2x sustained for 30m -> rollback.

Priya (Eng): +1 on per-route P99. also need explicit acceptance tests for cold-starts and shift to smaller quantized variants when load spikes. propose fallback order: 1) prefix cache hit, 2) smaller quantized model (same weights), 3) route to dedicated pool, 4) degrade to limited tokens w/ user-facing notice.

Liam (ML): we should specify quality acceptance too — we can't silently switch to much lower quality. suggest tie a simple eval run during canary: sample 1k prompts, check BLEU/embedding similarity/regression thresholds. If quality delta > 5% on critical prompts -> block automatic fallback.

Jordan (Product): acceptance criteria (draft) for launch PRD:
- Canary: 6h at 10% traffic across two regions, min 50k requests/sample distribution
- Stability: no rollback triggers during canary; if rollback happens, classify cause and re-run
- Latency: P95 <= 200ms, P99 <= 1s during canary for targeted routes
- Error budget: < 0.05% daily observed during canary
- Quality: no more than 5% regressed prompts on eval set

Sam (SRE): add: alerting + playbook must be in place for canary. playbook snippet:
```
if error_budget_burn > 2x for 30m -> notify pager, pause rollout, trigger fallback routing, and start incident runbook.
if P99 > threshold AND error_budget_burn > 1.5x -> auto-scale and notify.
```

Priya (Eng): implementation notes: KV cache warm-up will skew early canary numbers. acceptance must require warm starts (e.g., first 30m excluded) or warm-up traffic synthetic step. also add test for prefix cache invalidation when model variant changes.

canary-bot: Canary started @1903456900: sending 10k synthetic requests across us-west/us-east, seq_len distribution sampled from prod. 0 errors in first 5m, P95=160ms, P99=520ms.

Liam (ML): good to see numbers. please capture model-specific metrics (kvcache hit rate, kv miss latency) in canary dashboard. if kvcache hit < 70% -> baseline comparisons might not be valid.

Anya (PM): edge cases to call out in PRD acceptance: multi-region failover (traffic shift), long-tail token storms (one user sending long contexts), and partial-function-calls when model times out. include explicit owner for each path.

Jordan (Product): on customer asks — enterprise wants SLA language. propose: SLA ties to availability metric only, excludes maintenance windows and force-majeure, and has a per-month credit formula for >0.1% downtime. legal will review but we need numbers in PRD.

Sam (SRE): operationally, we need a fallback policy table in PRD:
- Severity 1: total region outage -> failover to secondary region, reduce max tokens to 256, enable aggressive batching
- Severity 2: sustained P99 degradation -> route to quantized variant, notify customers on status page
- Severity 3: isolated errors -> retry with jitter up to 2x then surface error to client

Priya (Eng): acceptance test matrix (high level):
- Load: 2x normal traffic for 1h -> maintain P95 threshold
- Bust: KV cache flush -> P95 change within 20% and no >1% error spike
- Quality: eval harness run with no >5% critical regressions
- Canary: pass criteria as Jordan listed

Anya (PM): ok action items:
- Anya: update PRD with SLO table, fallback policies, and acceptance tests (today)
- Priya: add cache warm-up and variant switch tests to CI (owner)
- Sam: draft playbook + thresholds + SLO burn alert rules
- Liam: provide eval set + automated check for canary
- Jordan: coordinate legal for SLA wording and credits

Priya (Eng): noted. I'll also add a short runbook for the model-variant switch to avoid cache poisoning.

Sam (SRE): I'll prototype the burn-rate detection rule in staging and share alerts tonight.

Anya (PM): thanks all. i'll update the PRD and ping for a quick review. if anyone objects to the thresholds above, now's the time. otherwise i'll mark as draft-accepted and attach canary schedule. :thumbsup:
